entries.title: Proverbs 23:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Ruler - With a great man.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Put a knife - Restrain thine appetite, as if a man stood with a knife at thy throat.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Deceitful - They do not yield thee that satisfaction which thou didst expect from them.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thine own wisdom - From worldly wisdom, which persuades men to use all possible means to get riches.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Set thine eyes - Look upon it with earnestness and desire. Is not - Which has no solid and settled being. Eagle - Swiftly, strongly, and irrecoverably.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Evil eye - Of the envious or covetous man.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: So is he - You are not to judge of him by his words, but by the constant temper of his mind.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Vomit up - When thou perceivest his churlish disposition, his meat will be loathsome to thee. Sweet words - Thy pleasant discourse wherewith thou didst design to delight and profit him.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Of a fool - Cast not away good counsels upon incorrigible sinners.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Enter not - To possess their lands.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Redeemer - Heb. their near kinsman, to whom it belongs to avenge their wrongs, and to recover and maintain their rights.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shall not die - It is a likely way to prevent his destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My reins - I shall rejoice with all my soul.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: An end - An expected and happy end for such as fear God.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Guide - Order the whole course of thine affections and actions. In the way - In God's way.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Buy - Purchase it upon any terms, spare no pains or cost. Truth - The true and saving knowledge of God's will. Sell it not - Do not forsake it for any worldly advantage.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Give me - Solomon here speaks in God's name.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:30
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Mixt wine - Either mixed with water, or with other ingredients to make it strong and delicious.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Red - Which was the colour of the best wines in that country. Aright - When it sparkles, and seems to smile upon a man.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:34
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Lieth down - To sleep. Sea - In a ship in the midst of the sea.

entries.title: Proverbs 23:35–24:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sick - I was not sensible of it. Again - At present my condition requires sleep to settle myself, and when I am composed, I purpose to return to my former course.
